title: Text animation
purpose: Measures how text enters, emphasises, idles and exits (pop scale, overshoot, duration, easing, stagger) frame by frame.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F8 frame steps over every text entrance you measure; measure bbox height per frame on the stepped frames.
pitfalls: Measuring durations in frames without converting by the real fps
Generalising one animation to all text
Confusing a camera zoom with a text scale animation

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.parameter: one IR parameter object (name, type, description, default, min/max or choices, derived_from)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"

questions.question: How do captions enter (scale pop, fade, slide, typewriter, mask wipe, no animation)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds the caption entrance to motion.text_animations.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frame steps over the first 0.3 s of 4 caption cards; look at size, opacity and position per frame.
questions.challenge: Check at least 4 cards; one dramatic card is not the rule.

questions.question: How long does a caption entrance take (ms from first visible frame to settled)?
questions.how_to_answer: Count frames on F8 steps from first visible to stable size/position; ms = frames x 1000 / fps.
questions.challenge: Use the real fps from A7; report frames and ms.

questions.question: Does the entrance overshoot (scale above final size, then settle), and what is the peak scale?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills pop_scale_peak; springy overshoot was a liked reference trait in this project.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure text block height on each F8 frame; peak scale = max height / settled height.
questions.challenge: Report the height series; camera zoom during the same frames would contaminate it.

questions.question: How do captions exit (cut, fade, scale down, slide out), and how long does it take?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps over the last 0.3 s before 4 caption changes.
questions.challenge: If the next caption replaces the old one on the same frame, the exit is a cut.

questions.question: When a key word pops, how many ms after (or before) the spoken word does the pop start?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the keyword pop sync offset.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 at emphasised words versus the word onset on A1 spectrogram.
questions.challenge: Report n and spread; the word onset must be read from audio, not caption timing.

questions.question: How does the title enter and how long does its entrance take?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 at the title's first appearance.
questions.challenge: Compare with hook_first_seconds-015; disagreements must be explained.

questions.question: How do item labels (for example FACT N) enter (slam with scale-down, slide, flip, pop, fade)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 at 3 label appearances.
questions.challenge: Check all 3 match.

questions.question: How are key numbers revealed (count-up, flip, scale pop, typewriter, static)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 over the number's first 0.6 s; a count-up shows intermediate values.
questions.challenge: Intermediate values must be visible on at least 2 frames for count-up.

questions.question: Is there a stagger between words or lines entering, and how many ms apart?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps across multi-word entrances; time between successive word appearances.
questions.challenge: Word-by-word captions timed to speech are not a stagger; a stagger is faster than speech.

questions.question: What easing curve does the text motion follow (spring with overshoot, ease-out-back, ease-out, linear)?
questions.how_to_answer: Plot the scale or position series from F8 steps; overshoot then settle with oscillation = spring; single overshoot = ease-out-back.
questions.challenge: Report the series values; the curve name must match them.

questions.question: Does text move while it is on screen (idle float, breathing scale, wobble)?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare text bbox across F1 frames 0.5 s apart within one card.
questions.challenge: A camera move that includes the text layer must be excluded; check if the background shifts the same way.

questions.question: Is motion blur or squash-and-stretch applied to moving text?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frames mid-animation; look for smeared or non-uniformly scaled glyphs.
questions.challenge: Compression smear is not motion blur; it appears as blocks.

questions.question: What share of text entrances land within 80 ms of a music onset?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a beat-sync rule for text.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare entrance times (from F8 or text_regions) with evidence.audio.onsets_s.
questions.challenge: Compare with the chance rate given onset density.

questions.question: Are text entrances accompanied by a sound effect (pop, click, whoosh)?
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrogram with highpass around 4 entrances.
questions.challenge: Speech consonants are transient; the sfx must not coincide with a word onset.

questions.question: Are there highlight sweeps, underlines being drawn, or boxes drawing around words?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 at emphasised moments.
questions.challenge: List timestamps for each.

questions.question: Are mask reveals used (text wiping in behind an edge)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps: partial letters cut by a straight edge.
questions.challenge: A slide from outside the frame is not a mask reveal.

questions.question: Is rotation used in text entrances, and by how many degrees?
questions.how_to_answer: Measure baseline angle on F8 frames.
questions.challenge: Report the angle per frame.

questions.question: What share of text elements animate at all?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator whether to animate everything or only key elements.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify 10 text appearances as animated or not.
questions.challenge: Report the sample.

questions.question: What fraction of a caption card's time is spent animating versus static and readable?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a readability constraint for animation length.
questions.how_to_answer: (entrance ms + exit ms) / card duration for 5 cards.
questions.challenge: Use the same cards for all terms.

questions.question: Is the text itself the main visual (kinetic typography) for any section?
questions.how_to_answer: Find shots where text covers more than 30% of the frame and moves in layout (F2).
questions.challenge: A large static title card is not kinetic typography.

questions.question: Is the same animation used for the same element type throughout (consistency)?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare entrance type per element role across 3 instances each.
questions.challenge: Report which instances were compared.

questions.question: How does one caption card give way to the next (instant replace, cross-fade, push, exit then enter with a gap)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 across 4 caption changes.
questions.challenge: Check 4 changes.

questions.question: How many frames does a typical text entrance take at the source frame rate?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a frame-exact value for renderers working in frames.
questions.how_to_answer: Frame count from F8 steps; report fps.
questions.challenge: Variable frame rate sources make frame counts unreliable; check A7 for avg vs real frame rate.

questions.question: Is there a shine or glint pass across the title or labels?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 on the title: a bright band moving across letters.
questions.challenge: A light-leak layer over everything is not a text shine.

questions.question: Is text shaken or vibrated for emphasis, and with what amplitude?
questions.how_to_answer: Track text bbox position across F8 frames.
questions.challenge: Report px amplitude.

questions.question: What should pop_scale_peak and pop_ms be as parameters, with ranges from the evidence?
questions.how_to_answer: Default = observed medians (003, 002); range = observed min/max.
questions.challenge: Ranges wider than observed must be marked assumed.

questions.question: Write the caption animation rule (entrance, keyword pop, exit) in terms of parameters.
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a procedural animation.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine 001-005, for example 'enter: scale 0.85 to pop_scale_peak to 1.0 over pop_ms with ease-out-back; key word pops 1.0 to 1.12 to 1.0 over 180 ms at word onset; exit: cut'.
questions.challenge: Every number in the rule must come from a measurement or be marked as a default.

questions.question: Do text elements enter from a consistent direction or along a consistent axis?
questions.how_to_answer: From F8 steps, note entrance direction for 6 elements.
questions.challenge: Report the counts per direction.

questions.question: Does the backing panel animate separately from the text (panel first, text after), and with what offset?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps at caption or title starts.
questions.challenge: Report frames and ms.

questions.question: Is animation applied per character, per word, or per line?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 steps: see which units move independently.
questions.challenge: Check one long caption.

questions.question: Is there a gap or overlap between one caption leaving and the next appearing (ms)?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 across 4 changes: frames with no caption (gap) or two captions (overlap).
questions.challenge: Report the sign convention and n.

questions.question: Is there anticipation before a pop (a brief scale-down before the scale-up)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds anticipation to the pop curve.
questions.how_to_answer: Height series from F8 just before emphasised words.
questions.challenge: Report the height series.
